first-pass.description: Headline systems at three loads x 5 runs, then each ablation at 100% load x 3 runs. Ordered so a budget stop keeps the most valuable cells.

under-20h.description: Headline systems at 100% load x 5 and 125% x 3, then each ablation at 100% load x 3, then, only if the time budget remains, one 50% load run each for layover-combined and vllm as a low-load sanity check. Last in order, so a budget stop drops them first and the report lists them as not run.

three-loads-lean.description: Headline systems at all three loads x 3, 100% first, then each ablation at 100% load x 2.

final.description: What a $10 GPU budget buys on one 24 GB card: Layover against vLLM at 100% load x 2 on the first 15 tasks, then layover-discard x 2. The CPU tier is 24 GiB for every system. SGLang is left out for the budget.

final-ablations.description: final, then keep_ttl and swap at 100% load x 2, run into final's results only when money remains after it.

runpod-l4.description: For one rented L4 container with about 50 GB of RAM and about 15 GPU hours in all. The CPU tier is 24 GiB for every system, so the pinned memory fits beside the server. Layover and vLLM at 100% and 125% load x 3, then SGLang at the same points, then each ablation at 100% load x 2. Ordered so a budget stop keeps the most valuable cells.

full.description: first-pass, then the synthetic sweeps over tool latency and branching, kept for later.

selection.method: Chosen with bench/run_matrix.py --sweep-separation: the real scheduler on a virtual clock at estimate_assumptions and swap_s_per_token (about 20 GB/s), over one seed per run. These are simulated, assumed rates, never results. A point stays if, at each rung vLLM is expected to choose, Layover's combined policy beats discard with its radix tree on (a stand-in for a prefix cache with no working CPU tier) by min_gap in every run, with early demotions in the median run. 12 jobs barely filled the pool, so 40 jobs replaced them. Tool 8 s was dropped: at 40 jobs its gap was about 1.02 at these rungs, since long tool waits spread the load out, and 4 s fell short too at about 1.08 to 1.14. Combined and swap stay within about 3% of each other at every point, so these lines show keeping KV against losing it, not the combined policy against swap. expected_rates_per_s come from simulating the ladder on the reference point: 0.4 with offload inert (discard stand-in), 0.8 with offload working (swap stand-in).

calibration.definition: the arrival rate at which vLLM's mean JCT reaches target_slowdown times its unloaded mean JCT, on the full headline workload with warm-up jobs excluded. Unloaded is unloaded_jobs measured jobs, each run alone; a rung's mean is those same jobs in that rung, so the ratio is not one of two job mixes. The rate is log-interpolated between the two ladder rungs that bracket the crossing. A ladder that never crosses, or starts past it, stops the matrix unless --accept-saturation-edge is passed, and then every output says so.
calibration.expected_saturation_method: SIMULATED, never a result: the real scheduler on a virtual clock over the 30 prepared trajectories with their recorded tool times, at estimate_assumptions. 0.025 jobs/s with vLLM's offload inert (discard with the prefix cache on as its stand-in) and 0.034 with it working (swap as its stand-in). The knee is sharp, so the rungs are close around it and the walk starts between them; for planning hours only.
